scenario.name: AWS CIRT & CISA Cloud DFIR — AWS IAM PassRole + Lambda Privilege Escalation & StopLogging Tampering
scenario.overview: Think of a classic neighborhood post office with brass P.O. boxes lining the back wall, a parcel scale counter, a blue street mailbox outside, and angled mail sorting chutes. At the neighborhood post office counter, a sender slips tiny coded lines onto the back of ordinary postcards and drops them one by one into the mail sorting slot. In this real-world scenario, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass p.o. box sorting wall, then smuggles copied records out past the postal scale & stamp window in tiny disguised batches. The postmaster reviews the evening dispatch ledger and spots hundreds of oddly coded postcards all mailed to the exact same remote P.O. box. In this scenario (T1098.001, AWS CIRT & CISA Cloud DFIR, AWS IAM PassRole + Lambda Privilege Escalation & StopLogging Tampering), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: iAM Privilege Escalation via iam:PassRole +, then lambda Invocation, then cloudTrail Anti-Forensics Attempt Blocked. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering IAM Privilege Escalation via iam:PassRole +, then Lambda Invocation, then CloudTrail Anti-Forensics Attempt Blocked, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on SIEM Event 201 correlated across the documented kill chain.
